sekibune.hull.towerProvenance: The WALLED form is attested: the Busan boat-barrier scroll of 1593 (Univ. of Tokyo), this card's own plate, draws the yakata as a closed plank house with a ridged roof on hull after hull — the open pavilion drawn before round 117 was the class default (the panokseon's janggundae), not this plate. The PLAN is derived: no Sengoku sekibune survives, so the 4.5 x 2.8 m footprint, the 2.0 m eaves and the roof pitch are read off the scroll's hulls at ship scale — good to the nearest half metre, no finer. The scroll also hangs cloth in the wall openings of several cabins; since round 139 one opening a side is drawn with the cloth hung in it. The OPENING's size and place are derived — no cabin interior is attested, and the scroll resolves the openings only to ship scale — the cloth itself is the scroll's.
sekibune.hull.makuProvenance: The CLOTH is attested: the Busan boat-barrier scroll of 1593, this card's own plate, hangs a white band under a dark scalloped hem along the yagura band on hull after hull of the anchored fleet, and the atakebune amidships wears the same dress inverted — dark with white scallops — under sail. The scroll draws NO plank belt at this band, so gunDeck.walls (the panokseon's sangjang belt, round 118) is refuted for this class by its own plate. The DIMENSIONS are derived: the scroll stretches the upperworks, so the band's depth in metres cannot be read off it — the drawn cloth fills the band the model's own rail and deck bound, and the ~0.7 m scallop bay (makuBayM) is read off the scroll at its ~16 px/m (a ~25 m hull drawn ~400 px long), good to the nearest half metre, no finer. The BORDER's place and cut are the plate's own: on every hull that resolves it — the atakebune above all, the same dress at better scale — the scallops hang from the band's HEAD, tangent, cut from one strip, white cusps rising between them to the hanging line; until round 170 the drawn valance hung spaced discs off the band's FOOT, the record's own sentence inverted. The drawn valance is one strip a side, contiguous semicircles of half the recorded bay; its depth (a semicircle's, half the bay) is a class default — the scroll's stretch bars a finer read. Whether a sekibune cruised with the maku hung is not attested — the scroll's fleet is anchored, the atakebune wears hers under sail — and the ends of the band are left open: the plate shows the cloth only in broadside.
sekibune.hull.samaProvenance: The SLOTS are attested for the class: Japanese accounts of the sekibune have the so-yagura walled with tate-ita shield planks pierced by sama, firing slots for bow and arquebus — the wall's purpose on a hull that mounts no broadside. The COUNT, SIZE and HEIGHT are derived: no Sengoku sekibune survives, and the Busan scroll (~16 px/m) resolves the yagura band but not individual slots, so 13 a side is set from the oar-station rhythm the length itself is derived from, and each slot is drawn 0.10 m wide by 0.36 m tall, centred 0.90 m over the fighting deck — the height a man standing on that deck fires from. Since round 140 the slots are OPENINGS cut through the drawn plank, with reveal faces the plank's own thickness deep and a dark board behind each so the slot reads into the deck's shadow; before that each was a dark plate laid on the wall's face.
sekibune.hull.windlassProvenance: JUDGED SILENT, r176 — the windlass question for this hull, opened by the r172 residual, closes with nothing drawn, and this field says why. Her tradition's machine is the rokuro, and it is not a windlass: the surviving spindle and the Hokyu-maru model at the Minamichita wasen museum (photographs read this round, form only, no scale on the pages) show a vertical tapered spindle standing between a lower deck and an overhead beam, two long bars passed through it crosswise at different heights, the rope winding at its foot. Both fetched descriptions place and rig it the same way: two sets inside the aft yagura house, the line from the masthead semi block over the stern tobi-guruma block, winding yard, tender and anchor from within the ship (Minamichita wasen museum; Museum of Maritime Science monoshiri sheet 28). Every attestation is the Edo cargo tradition — the bezaisen, a type that postdates this drawn ship — and the museum's own sentence treats the machine's installation aboard as a development within that tradition. No fetched source puts a rokuro, or any winch, on a sekibune or any Sengoku warship; the Murakami Suigun Museum states the sekibune and kobaya barely appear in contemporary documents or drawings at all. Drawing one would stack three unsourced inferences: era (1597 against Edo attestations), class (cargo to war, with no textual bridge like the Tiangong Kaiwu's statement that the ocean transport's gear was all the same), and placement (the attested stand is inside an aft working house between floor and beam; this ship's aft house is the commander's yakata). The record stays silent and the builder draws nothing. That her hands hoisted by direct pull is itself an inference, marked as one on the card. Scope: this judgment is for the drawn 1597 instance; the class ran to 1868, an Edo sekibune shares the attested machine's own era, and a drawn Edo instance would reopen the question.
sekibune.hull.anchorProvenance: The PRESENCE and the FORM are the plate's and the era's. The card's own plate — the Busan boat-barrier scroll of 1593, Univ. of Tokyo — draws the anchored fleet riding to twisted cables and, at the barrier line's upper and lower ends, the anchor itself at the cable's end: stockless, short-shanked, four strongly recurved claws (crops read r187; the lower one is clipped at the sheet edge). The era and class evidence agrees and points at her: on Ishii Kenji's evidence (1983, via Matsui Hironobu, Kanazawa Univ. archaeology bulletin 34, 2013, the four-claw iron anchor's typological study) — the anchor drawn in the 1433 Jingu Kogo engi emaki, and the 1486 Boshi nyuminki recording iron anchors on the Ming embassy ships — warships and special ships carried the four-claw iron anchor alongside wood-stone anchors from the first half of the 15th century, while wood and stone stayed the ordinary wasen's mainstay until the mid-17th: an early-1600s Osaka screen counts one iron anchor to eight wood-stone. The NAME and the making are the wasen tradition's: the Minamichita wasen museum's sentence — a square iron bar, its tip split in four and the quarters bent outward into claws, the count varying with the ship's size — and the Tomo anchor-smiths' recorded process (Tamura 1978, via Matsui). Every DIMENSION is a named default: no sekibune anchor survives. The drawn 2.0 m overall sits inside Matsui's measured corpus of 49 survivors (1.05–3.03 m, nearly all Edo–Meiji), at the corpus's own small/large break — about 120 kg by the Kozushima seabed anchor's calibration (2.8 m raised at 330–340 kg), a direct-pull load for a crew whose rokuro is judged silent (r176); ring and arm proportions follow the corpus and Matsui's fig. 1. The plate is at ship scale (~16 px/m) and no dimension is taken from it. COUNT is not recorded: one is drawn; Ishii's sentence has iron used alongside wood-stone on the warships, and that mixed tackle is not drawn — no count or mix is attested for her class. The STOW is a placement inference, the fleet rule (r182–r186): recovered on the open foredeck forward of the so-yagura — the bow is where the tradition works its anchor: the Edo bezaisen rests it on the uwakannuki, a hard-oak member on the bow's topmost rail, and belays the cable there (Minamichita, the same page; that beam is Edo cargo structure and is not drawn) — rolled 45 degrees, pitched to the deck's own gradient, settled by measured box; the cable bent to the free accessory ring and flaked in a coil beside it — no belay is attested and she has no winding machine. A measured Sengoku warship anchor, or the 1433 emaki plate in resolution, replaces the defaults and this field says so. Member sections are the corpus's own record, read r191: 表1 of the same paper (Matsui 2013 p.38) measures all 49 anchors at member level, and the arms are RECTANGULAR forged bars — 最大幅×最大厚 at the root, a wide thin blade at the fluke tip. Corpus means for the 27 consistently-printed anchors ≥190 cm, as fractions of 全長: root 0.0346±0.0037 × 0.0198±0.0033, tip 0.0220±0.0052 × 0.0058±0.0031. Both rings take the type anchor the class already cites (Onominato a: teardrop 44×19 cm of 3 cm bar, accessory ring ⌀36 of 4×4.5 section, on 269 cm). The weight field kg 122 is DERIVED by cube-law from the corpus's one weighed anchor — the Kozushima wreck anchor, 2.8 m, 330–340 kg by forklift (約90貫), raised 1990 — 15.26 kg per m³ of 全長³. The shank's two stations are the Pacific corpus's own calipers, read r192: 表3 of 二宮俊洋's master's survey (東京海洋大学 2014, oacis record 1018 — 144 anchors, Ibaraki to Wakayama, the companion survey to Matsui's) records the shank per anchor at the clean upper bar (軸正面×軸側面) and at the root boss where the four arms are forged on (軸根本正面×軸根本側面). Corpus means as fractions of 全長, each anchor's pair sorted (min,max) because the shrine's mounting sets which face is 正面: upper bar 0.0214±0.0046 × 0.0303±0.0058 (n=17), root boss 0.0491±0.0072 × 0.0764±0.0099 (n=16); excluded by name №1 (sea-concreted, every member ~2× corpus), №74 (exfoliated to 0.012 of 全長) and №93 (printed-inconsistent, a 0.36·全長 root), and №82's shaft pair flagged (側面/正面 = 2.8, twice anyone else) and dropped. The r191 CONTEST is RESOLVED, in the record's favour on both sides: the monument photographs' 0.023–0.034 was the upper bar, and the old solve's 0.047 was the root boss (0.0491) — the real shank tapers hard from an oblong boss to a slender near-square bar, and both prior readings were right at their own stations. The drawn shank now carries exactly those stations; the knee where the taper meets the bar is the one dimension no table records, SOLVED so the drawn iron weighs the record's kg at 7850 kg/m³ — at (2.0 m, 122 kg) it lands at 77% of the shank, inside the drawn form's own solvable band (69–138 kg); a record outside that band would clamp the knee and the mass audit would convict, a contest and not a knob. Cross-corpus check on the members already held: №71 (銚子, 300 cm) calipers claw root 0.0350×0.0233 and claw length 0.320 of 全長 against Matsui's 0.0346×0.0198 and the drawn 0.30 — two independent coasts agree on the arms. Residual: the mass calibration still hangs on the Kozushima weighing alone (約90貫 by forklift); the 1993 site report (東京都教育委員会, per the nabunken bibliography — print only, not surfaced open) would firm the kg, no longer the shank. The audit holds the drawn iron to the record's weight (V-YMASS, 12%) and the drawn shank's end sections to the calipered stations (V-YSHANK, 12%).

great-eastern.hull.deck.provenance: RECORDED: the contemporary descriptions carry it twice over - Description and History of the Great Eastern (1861): 'the massive wrought-iron deck is covered with teak planking', and of the cellular structure, 'the deck, which is of teak planking placed over the top plates, forms the upper surface of the tube'. The deck beneath is Brunel's double cellular iron top on the Britannia-bridge principle, two half-inch plates top and bottom on longitudinal webs (Descriptive Particulars of the Great Eastern Steam Ship, 1857) - so the teak is a covering laid over iron, which is what this model draws. No plank dimensions are attested; the drawn planks are class defaults.

clipper.hull.headProvenance: Type-period CLASS DEFAULT, no hull-specific plate: the tea clipper of 1869 carried a clipper bow, the knee of the head under the bowsprit with trailboards and a figurehead (Cutty Sark, 1869, as preserved); grade 1, the single rail.

yamato.hull.deck.provenance: RECORDED, species CONTESTED: Skulski (Anatomy of the Ship - The Battleship Yamato) gives hinoki, Japanese cypress, planks 127 x 76 mm; the Yamato Museum, Kure, states the ship's deck timber was Taiwanese cypress. carrier.hull.rakeProvenance: loa 337.0 is the ship's EXTREME length - 1,106 ft, the figure Commander, Naval Air Force Atlantic gives for USS Gerald R. Ford - and it is not a shell length: the flight deck is its own attested plate at 1,092 x 256 ft (333 x 78 m), and no source publishes the shell's length between extremities. The rakes 0.03/0.02 are reconstruction; the drawn planking spans 333.85, INSIDE the record's loa. The deck is drawn at flightDeckLen 333.0, anchored so the aft round-down overhangs the fantail and the span from the shell's bow tip to the round-down is 337.00 = loa exactly. A planking-only sweep reads -3.15 on this hull by construction; that is the record's geometry, not an under-fill.
carrier.hull.islandSideProvenance: ATTESTED: the Ford's island stands at the starboard deck edge abaft amidships and her landing area is angled to port — the arrangement of every angled-deck carrier, stated in this record's own text and on the class's page (Wikipedia, Gerald R. Ford-class aircraft carrier, accessed 2026-08-03). The word drives every one-sided fitting through the builder's islandSide(): the island, the two deck-edge lifts and the hangar doors under them, the catapults, the foul line and the deck park stand on this side, and the landing area runs forward to the other. Until r270 each was drawn at +z under the belief that +z was starboard; +z is port (build/staging/r254/side.json, the frame's own statement at the head of hull.js), so the whole arrangement was the ship's mirror. The audit reads this word and the meshes, not the builder (D-ISLAND-SIDE).

container.hull.freeboardProvenance: TYPE SHIP — the drawn freeboard is DERIVED, and the card row says so (rule 10). This composite is drawn at the 24,000-TEU generation its own rows name (MSC Gülsün / MSC Irina classes, 399.9 m × 61.3 m): depth moulded 33.2 m to main deck (RINA, Significant Ships of 2019, MSC Gülsün; the Irina class repeats the figure) less the recorded 16.0 m deep draught leaves 17.2 m of weather-deck freeboard. The old 30.0 had no source and stood the deck at nearly the whole moulded depth over the water — a hull floating near her light line drawn as loaded. The statutory summer freeboard is smaller still and is measured to a lower freeboard deck, not the weather deck this model lofts — the same distinction ever-given's stationProvenance records from her casualty report.
container.hull.rakeProvenance: AUTHORED to fill the record's own allowance: loa 399.9 − lwl 383.0 = 16.9 m, and the old 0.03/0.0 drew only 12.0 m of it (r129 fleet sweep, −4.9). 383.0 is the class's length between perpendiculars (RINA, Significant Ships of 2019, MSC Gülsün — the same plate as the depth moulded above); on this generation the transom stands nearly plumb at the aft perpendicular and virtually the whole LOA−LPP difference is the flared bow above the bulb — ever-given, the fleet's attested hull of the same 400 m generation, carried the identical 383 LBP against 399.94 LOA before r113 moved her lwl to her casualty report's 387 waterline. The stern keeps its authored 0.0 and the stem takes the allowance: 0.0423, which the r129 loft clamp trims to 16.90 m of bow overhang, 399.90 m drawn exactly. NOTE the semantics this leaves: this type ship's lwl is the class LBP; the loaded waterline of the real hull runs ~4 m further over the bulb (the ever-given precedent) and is not published for this class, so the record keeps the figure a plate attests.

ever-given.hull.rakeProvenance: The lwl 387.00 this record carries is the LBP her own casualty report states (PMA R-026-2021-DIAM, the same plate stationProvenance reads), and the transom stands near-plumb at the AP on this 400 m generation (sternRake 0 - the class geometry r131 sourced from the MSC Gulsun plate, RINA Significant Ships of 2019). So the whole loa - lwl = 12.98 m allowance is the flared bow above the bulb. stemRake authored 0.0325, a hair over the exact 0.032452; the r129 clamp trims the drawn overhang to 12.98 m so planking spans 399.98 exactly.
ever-given.hull.stationProvenance: Twin-island stations from the ship's OWN papers, not a photograph: the PMA casualty report R-026-2021-DIAM carries her voyage-plan particulars (Fig. 6, loading computer) — keel to highest point 75.71 m, air draft 60.26 m at ~15.4 m draught, and the highest point (the bridge mast) 245.35 m forward of the aft perpendicular on LBP 387.00 m, which is u 0.366 from the FP; bridgeU 0.361 lands the drawn mast there. Depth moulded 32.90 m and breadth 58.80 m from the same report's Table 1 (vessel certificates); freeboard 17.2 = depth less the 15.7 m draught (the statutory 10.226 m summer freeboard is to a lower freeboard deck, not the weather deck the model draws). Funnel casing at funnelU 0.845 READ off the GA plan reproduced in the report (Fig. 2, 711x315 px, ~1.04 px/m — good to +/-4 m, no finer), cross-checked against Commons broadsides (kees torn 51343xxx series: dark-green casing amid the stacks, short black stack above). Stow: 23 rows on the real ship; the drawn TEU grid fits 22 across the 58.8 m beam (one row under, below any frame's resolution), 10 tiers on deck midships-aft per the Rotterdam photographs. EVERGREEN side lettering span and stern name from the same photographs; bow name NOT drawn — the flare there is curved and a flat decal would lie about it.

azzam.hull.boatsProvenance: INBOARD: her tenders stow in a garage within the hull, not on deck. The design accounts record the concept grew from 145 m to 180.6 m partly to make room for tenders, fuel and machinery inside (Nauta design history via Boat International and YachtBuyer, which lists her tender garage), and the delivery photograph on this card shows a bare topside — no boat stands on any deck. Her tender complement is not published, so no count is claimed.
azzam.hull.cluster.provenance: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-16 off a clean broadside (Wikimedia Commons, File:Azzam IMO 9693367 S Bremen 09-05-2014.jpg, Wolfgang Fricke, CC BY 3.0) with the stem, transom and waterline as the three anchors and her recorded 180.6 m as the scale — 8.33 px per metre. Her house is FOUR decks, not five: the crest reads 21 m over the water against the five-deck stack's 24.25. AFT DOMES CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (round 97): a strip scan at 17.8-23.0 m over the water, anchors x332/x1950/y941 at 8.96 px/m, finds white mass aft of the block only at u 0.700-0.721 (the 3.4 m pair) and 0.731-0.744 (the 2.2 m single) — nothing stands at the earlier 0.763/0.803, which would float past the fairing foot now that tier 2's wall is measured to end there. azzam.hull.tierBands.provenance: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-17 off the kept broadside (File:Azzam IMO 9693367 S Bremen 09-05-2014.jpg, Wolfgang Fricke, CC BY 3.0) at 8.96 px/m with stem x332 / transom x1950 / waterline y941 as anchors. The glazing is not a continuous ribbon: each tier carries GROUPS of punched lights with long blank wall runs between, different per tier. groups[tier] = [uStart, uEnd, pitchM, pierFrac]; pitchM 0 is one continuous run. Tier 0: six 4.1 m lights at 6.1 m pitch forward, small lights amidships, a 23 m run aft. Tier 1: four 3.2 m lights forward, small lights, a long aft run. Tier 2: a 10 m forward run and a short aft group under the fairing. Crest: the raked front glass and one aft run. AFT EXTENTS CORRECTED round 97: the r96 row scan read dark BACKGROUND over the stepped-down stern as glazing, because with every tier drawn ~3 m the walls were assumed to reach the old aft edges — the silhouette envelope shows tier 0's wall ends at u 0.82, tier 1's at 0.795, tier 2's at the fairing foot 0.744 and the crest's at the block face 0.708, so the groups that ran past those edges (t0 to 0.93, t1 to 0.889, t2 to 0.822, crest to 0.745) are trimmed or dropped. What stands aft of each wall is open terrace, and glazing there is UNKNOWN, not asserted. bandsM[tier] = [sill, head] in metres over the waterline, straight from the plate: 10.9-12.6 / 14.8-16.7 / 18.1-19.5 / 21.2-22.4 — the crest head read 22.8 exceeds the 22.5 roof by less than the read noise and is clipped under it.
azzam.hull.hullRows.provenance: READ 2026-08-17 off the same broadside at 8.96 px/m. The freeboard is not bare: an upper row of ~1.0 m rectangular windows, sills 4.9 m and heads 6.9 m over the waterline, in five clusters at ~1.9 m pitch between u 0.26 and 0.49, with two dark side doors aft of them; a low porthole line, ~0.45 m glasses about 3.0 m over the water, in clusters of three or four between u 0.25 and 0.52 plus one forward at u 0.11; and a long tinted band 8.2-8.7 m over the water under the aft deck edge, broken once, u 0.60-0.77. azzam.hull.housePlateProvenance: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-17 (round 97) off the kept broadside at 8.96 px/m, by reading the upper silhouette envelope column by column with a ship-white classifier rather than matching window rows. The aft staircase was previously misattributed by two tiers because every tier was drawn ~3 m and the real tiers are 4.5/3.9/2.6/2.5 m: the 0.821 edge is TIER 0's roof end (roof 13.5 m, visible terminating at u 0.819), 0.888 is the main-deck bulwark run-out, and tier 2's wall in fact ends at the fairing foot 0.744. tierFloorsM 13.5/17.4/20.0 and houseTopM 22.5 are the envelope's roof reads, each confirmed at two or more exposed spans fore and aft (tier 0: 13.3-13.7 fore, 13.5-13.8 aft; tier 1: 17.3-17.9 fore, 17.3-17.4 aft; tier 2: white to ~20 under the crest's raked glass; top = blockTopM). Aft of the house the stern terraces down — bulwark tops 9.7 m to u 0.90, then 6.9 (0.905-0.93), 6.3, 5.4, 4.5, 3.1 m at the transom — which the model does not yet build; the read is recorded here for when it does.
azzam.hull.formProvenance: READ off the same broadside at 8.33 px/m (File:Azzam IMO 9693367 S Bremen 09-05-2014.jpg, Wolfgang Fricke, CC BY 3.0). houseRamp: every tier front is raked so its head lands on the next front's foot, one continuous sweep from the foredeck to the crest, where the model had four vertical steps. faired: the topside between the waterline and the sheer is an unbroken gloss surface with no visible plate lands, tone patchwork or streaking anywhere along her 180.6 m. bowFlare 0.14: the topsides lean out over the fine entry; the plate cannot give a number at this bearing, so this is set to the smallest value that reads as flare in the bow capture and is marked DERIVED, not measured. capM 0.2: the dark strip at the deck edge measures 0.11-0.33 m on the broadside (median 0.2) where the model's beam-derived capping drew 0.53 m.
azzam.hull.sternSteps.provenance: MEASURED 2026-08-17 (round 98) off the kept broadside at 8.96 px/m, anchors x332/x1950/y941, silhouette envelope sampled every 0.0025 u (Research/segment-azzam-envelope.py). Aft of the house the stern descends in terraces, and the tops RAKE within each terrace - the silhouette is the outer bulwark cap, sweeping down toward each break: 9.9-9.6 m to the break at u 0.884 (the main-deck bulwark; round 97's coarser sampling read its run-out as 0.888), then 6.9-7.0 to 0.931, 6.6-6.1 to 0.946, 5.7-4.9 to 0.9625, 4.9-4.2 to 0.975, and 3.5-3.0 at the transom (flat 3.0 aft of u 0.9825). Occluders excluded from the read: the ensign u 0.83-0.87, davits or staff at 0.900, 0.9225, 0.930-0.9325 and 0.945-0.9475. topM [fwd, aft] is the measured cap line; deckM is DERIVED as the span's low cap minus a 0.9-1.0 m parapet, because the plate cannot see the decks behind their own bulwarks. The first span's deck is the hull's recorded 9.0 m sheer (deckM absent); its parapet is the 0.6-0.9 m the plate reads above it. ROUND 102: the 0.884 riser (the only full-height drop) now carries a tinted band and centreline doors - the delivery plate reads that face dark against the white, but its ~6.6 px/m cannot place panes, so the ARRANGEMENT is inferred. Twin flights close each lesser break, tops flush with the deck above; they stand behind the next bulwark aft, which is why the broadside envelope never saw them. No pool is drawn: none is attested at any measurable position.
azzam.hull.deck.provenance: RECORDED: the builder's specification as carried by the BOAT International Superyacht Directory entry for Azzam (Lurssen, 2013) - teak deck, steel hull, aluminium superstructure; press copy repeats 2,200 m2 of laid teak. Plank width and butt pattern are CLASS defaults for a yacht's laid teak (90 mm strakes), below what any plate of her can resolve.
azzam.hull.deck.roofsProvenance: TERRACES, NOT THE CREST: the 2,200 m2 of laid teak in the builder-sourced copy is far more area than her weather deck alone can carry on a 180.6 x 20.8 m hull, so her tier terraces carry the rest — which her photographs show. But the crest top is not among them: on the Klaus Jordan delivery-trials aerial (Lurssen press 2013, via CharterWorld wp-content, 960x640 copy, ~4.4 px/m locally at the crest — a colour-field read only, stated in Research/AZZAM-PLATES.md) the roof the radome cluster and mast stand on reads unbroken white coated plate, with the teak one level down on the ringing terraces. Pedestal base-plate detail is below that plate's resolution and is not claimed.
azzam.hull.paintProvenance: MEASURED off two independent broadsides — Wikimedia Commons File:AzzamCadiz.jpg (Javier Virues Ortega, CC BY-SA 4.0, port side, bow left) and File:Yacht Azzam - UAE.jpg (Farid mernissi, CC BY-SA 4.0, starboard, bow right). Both show her WHITE to the waterline with no boot-top and a near-black antifouling, where the class default for a hull built after 1955 is oxide red. And both show the deck edge rising about 3.0 m from amidships to the stem, against the 0.25 m the record carried — which is why she read as a flat slab. The RISE is a difference between two points on one line, so it is immune to where the hull ends and the first tier begins, which is the one thing these plates cannot resolve.
azzam.hull.sheerProvenance: MEASURED 2026-08-25 (round 160) off two independent broadsides, each with its scale: the Cadiz in-service broadside (Commons AzzamCadiz.jpg, 17.27 px/m re-anchored, stem tip x351 y1709, waterline fit y=1847.8+0.00162x) reads the stem head at 8.05-8.13 m and the foredeck cap 8.19-8.38 m rising to 8.84 at the house front; the kept Bremen broadside (azzam-broadside-fricke-2014.jpg, 8.96 px/m, anchors x332/x1950/y941) reads the same stem head at 8.37 m. Both refute the former sheerBow 3.0 (a 12.0 m bow) by ~3.9 m: her sheer is INVERTED, the bow below the freeboard deck, one sweep rising aft into the house. bowTopM is the two-plate band's centre; sheerBow = bowTopM - freeboard. The 1343_Azzam.jpg fitting-out oblique was rejected as a witness: no local scale anchor at the bow (Research/AZZAM-PLATES.md, r160 section).

endurance.hull.headProvenance: NO HEAD. The Framnaes longitudinal section (as Polaris, RMG J9266, web copy 1024x322 px, ~16.9 px/m along the hull) draws a straight raked stem, the 1.3 m baulk, with the bowsprit rising from the stemhead and no knee of the head, no headrail and no gammoning slot; Hurley's heeled plate (build/endurance-heeled.png, 1280x995 px, bow-on and foreshortened, so it bounds the shape and gives no station) shows the same plain stem under the bowsprit. The old record's head: 1 drew a pale cutwater knee standing 1.3 m before the stem, an S-curved headrail a side from the bow planking to the knee, and three turns of rope gammoning: an eighteenth-century head on a 1912 polar barquentine, in every bow view. r271 correction; the bowsprit keeps its bobstay.
endurance.hull.masts[2].boomFootProvenance: PLATE READ, r273/r275: the mizzen boom's jaws (the gooseneck) 4.0-4.3 m over the main deck at the mast, +/- 0.4, read off Hurley's plate from the starboard quarter (Commons a090007, State Library NSW, 1500x1124, ~24 px/m at the stern) in r273, where the boom lies against the mast above the deckhouse; the boom's rise aft (the cock) is NOT read from any plate of this ship and stands at the class minimum or at what the compass platform's box demands (the builder's derivation); a plate of her with the spanker set at a readable scale would replace both.
endurance.hull.helmProvenance: ON THE FLUSH MAIN DECK behind the bulwark, class station 0.94: the Framnaes section (RMG J9266, 1024x322, ~16.9 px/m, bow at the RIGHT) draws the deck line level to the counter, no poop; Hurley a090007 (starboard quarter, ~24 px/m aft) shows the wall solid to the counter and a man's head over the cap. r272's (0y61) closed as no fault, r273.
endurance.hull.fifeRail.provenance: NO PLATE SHOWS THE FOOT OF THE FORE MAST; the fife rail is drawn to CLASS figures (the rail 1.05 m over the deck, 0.10 over the pin rail; 0.55 m before the mast's skin and 0.85 m abaft it; 0.70 m off each side; posts 0.10 m square; a pin every 0.25 m; a U open aft), and the card says so. Plates read in r280, none of which reaches the foot: Hurley's deck plate (build/hurley-deck.jpg, 1200x858, the SLNSW flickr copy 3535443028 — Commons holds no larger) looks along the deck from amidships and the fore mast's foot stands behind the deck cargo, the winch drum and the kennels; the heeled plate (Commons 4793353650, 4776x3713, RMG P00004, from before the bow) and the Lichtbeelden Vereeniging lantern slide nr. 24 (Commons, 4117 px, the same heel from the port bow) show the bulwark's outside with the deck tilted away; RMG P00013 (4800 px, looking forward from the port bow) shows the cathead and the bow's bulwark only; the full-sail, night and broadside plates show the wall, which hides a waist-high rail. WHETHER THE COURSE HANGS IN JEERS AT ALL on a 1912 hull is itself unread: a lower yard of her date would commonly sit on an iron truss with chain slings, and the builder hangs it in jeers because the hull is wood (S.iron false) — a plate of her fore masthead at a readable scale, or the Framnaes rigging plan, would settle both. A plate of her foredeck from aft — Hurley's dogs-on-deck negatives at SLNSW or SPRI — is the first thing to fetch.
endurance.hull.aftPlatform.provenance: LATTICE PLATFORM WITH A HOODED BOX, read off Hurley a090007 (Commons, 1500x1124; ~24 px/m +/- 3 at the stern from the mast gaps; r273/a090007-stern-6x-ruled.png): cap top row 700, floor row 650 = 2.1 m (+/- 0.3) over the cap, 3.45 over the deck; frame 1.5 m wide, one cross-braced panel a face; box 0.8 x 1.0 m; centre col 910, 0.79 from the mizzen to the taffrail = u 0.99 +/- 0.02, an upper bound. Also in the heeled plate and, wrecked, in LCCN 2013646126. WHAT IT IS is inferred: a hooded box high and right aft is the standard compass on its platform, as Discovery, Nimrod and Terra Nova carried theirs; no source names Endurance's: CONTESTED. Centreline assumed. The rig lifts the mizzen boom over the box: level, its foot is 5.2 m over the deck at the mast, 0.5 m over the plate's gooseneck read (4.0-4.3 +/- 0.4); the cock is residual 0y63.
endurance.hull.stationProvenance: Masts, funnel, deckhouses and overhangs READ off the Framnaes longitudinal-section plan (as Polaris, RMG J9266, web copy 1024x322 px, ~16.9 px/m along the hull — stations good to ±0.5 m, no finer), anchored at the stem and counter LWL crossings; mast-gap ratio and funnel station cross-checked against the Hurley broadside (RMG P00018, ~12.6 px/m: fore-main/main-mizzen 1.12, funnel 45% of main→mizzen). Trucks from the same broadside at 12.6 px/m: fore 34.3 m, main 35.2 m, mizzen 29.3 m over the water, main the tallest — the old record drew the fore at 49 m (27.5 m lower through the square-stack rule) and the main at 31.7. Funnel at 0.677: the plan reads 0.670 +/- 0.015 and the boiler casing must seat inside the house whose forward end it rises from. Funnel black: it reads as dark as the black hull in every plate where masts read pale; height 5.7 m over the rail at the broadside’s scale. No forward deckhouse: the plan shows a boat on skids between fore and main, and no photograph shows a house there. Quarter boats (davitBoats): a canvas-covered boat hangs outboard in radial davits on the port quarter in the Hurley night plate and two stand on the starboard side in the full-sail plate; both plates are bow-on and foreshortened, so the station is bounded, not measured — abaft the aft house (plan, 0.781) and clear of the counter, u 0.80 ± 0.04. Length 6.7 m: the expedition's cutters (Dudley Docker, Stancomb Wills) as recorded; the James Caird measured 6.9. Kept: the forecastle break — the web plan at 16.9 px/m cannot carry a clean break station or height (the deck lines there are one to two px apart); needs the RMG original before it is modelled.
endurance.hull.deck.provenance: SOLID BULWARK, read off the Framnaes longitudinal section (as Polaris, RMG J9266, web copy 1024x322 px, ~16.9 px/m): at midships between the fore and main masts the cap rail's upper line lies at row 176-178 of the copy and the main deck's plank line at row 200, 22-24 px apart, so the bulwark stands 1.35 m (+/- 0.15) over the deck; the cap is drawn 5 px (0.3 m) deep, rows 178-183. The plates agree in kind and cannot give the height: Hurley's full-sail plate (build/hurley-fullsail.jpg, 2828x3912 px, from the port bow) shows a solid bulwark the whole length with a pale cap rail and a pale scrolled band under the cap at the bow; the night plate (build/hurley-night.jpg, 2590x3502 px) and the heeled plate (build/endurance-heeled.png) show the same wall with a lifebuoy hung on it; the beset broadside (RMG P00018, ~12.6 px/m) shows the cap line only, the hull behind ice. hull.freeboard is the SKIN's top in this record (the cap rail over the water, the r215 semantics): it was 2.0, the deck line's own height, and is 3.35 from r272, the cap's; the deck stays at 2.0 m over the water (deck.belowSheerM 1.35), so every mast, house, funnel and boat stands where it stood. The plan's own waterline, the long line at rows 236-238 that runs past both ends, lies 37 px (2.2 m) under the deck line and 44 px (2.6 m) over the keel's underside at row 281; the record's draught of 4.2 m does not match that, and the vertical scale of the web copy is unverified, so the draught is CONTESTED here and not changed (r272). The bulwark is the hull's own planking carried up to the cap, its inboard face the planking's back; stanchions, the pin rail and the scuppers are not drawn.

II figs 11-12 resolve six, period range 6-8). Form and proportions from Falconer 1769 CAPSTERN (whelps drumhead-to-deck like buttresses, chocks, two iron pawls, bars heaved at the breast) and pl.
